2) What would seniority-based routing (i.e., routing to senior ops on-call for Sev1s during business hours) cost versus a flat 24/7 NOC escalation?

Dana — great questions. Short answers first: yes, the priority path can be regional-only (reduces cost); and seniority-based routing is absolutely possible but carries a premium tied to on-call seniority band and guaranteed handoff SLAs.

I've attached a concise SLA table and an updated proposal (v2) with two paths:
- Priority Path (regional): reserved warm capacity + burst queue priority, 99.9% baseline for burst windows; priced as a % uplift on reserved capacity.
- Seniority Routing (business hours): routes Sev1 to named senior responders during M-F 8am–6pm PT; cheaper than 24/7 named senior coverage but still higher than standard escalation.

Tradeoffs to call out:
- Regional-only priority path is inexpensive but increases RTO risk for region-level outages — we recommend cross-region fallback for production-critical workloads.
- Seniority routing reduces time-to-ack but is manual and requires rotation commitments from your side for predictable coverage windows.

Proposed next step: I can put numbers on both options and a staged discount tied to commit (e.g., a 10% discount on the priority path with a 12-month committed spend). Will loop Marissa for pricing approval and Evelyn for operational runbook notes.

Best,
Karthik
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

For seniority routing, we recommend a hybrid: senior on-call M-F business hours + escalation to our dedicated NOC overnight. That keeps cost moderate and guarantees 24/7 page coverage.

Karthik — can you draft two pricing scenarios in the proposal:
A) Regional priority path + hybrid routing (recommended)
B) Cross-region priority + 24/7 senior named routing (premium)

Dana — can you confirm if procurement prefers vendor-owned named responders in the contract (we'll list names for the SOW) or a joint-responder model (BrightPath names primary responders and Redwood provides escalation engineering)? The billing implications differ.
